slides.title: Jamin
lines: Peer-to-peer trade escrow for Bitcoin Cash, written in SolidCash

slides.title: Jamin
lines: Sell BCH or PUSD to a stranger for local money. Neither side has to send first, and no exchange holds the coins.

items.text: Open jamin.sasateguh.com and choose Try it. The compiled contracts run on the SolidCash mock network in your browser.
Play seller, buyer, arbitrator or an outsider through release, buyer cancel, seller cancel and dispute. Each step shows the transaction or the contract's named error.
Let one panel member decide a dispute alone. The contract refuses until a second member signs.
Switch the seller to the demo wallet: the wallet pays and signs the seller's coins. The page is in English and Bahasa Melayu.
In a peer-to-peer trade one side has to send first, or both trust an exchange that holds the coins.
OpenPeer answered this on EVM with an MIT-licensed escrow contract. Jamin ports it to the Bitcoin Cash UTXO model in SolidCash.
Each escrow is a stateful contract: its state lives in the coin, and covenant rules fix every payout.
Building it turned up ten SolidCash issues. Three fixes are open as pull requests: #8, #9 and #10.
Nobody holds the coins in the middle. Every payout is a covenant output, so whoever builds the transaction cannot redirect it.
A dispute costs a fee from the side that opens it, and two of three named arbitrators decide it (checkMultiSig).
The seller can cancel only after the waiting time and only while the buyer has not marked the trade paid.
The same rules hold for BCH and for CashTokens such as PUSD.
92 SolidHat tests in 10 files. Removing a check from a copy of a contract makes its named test fail.
All five branches ran on a stock Bitcoin Cash Node 29.0.0 regtest node with mainnet relay rules: 20 transactions mined.
Largest unlocking script 6,888 of 10,000 bytes. Miner fees for all 20 transactions: 118,654 sats.
A seller wallet signing over the BCH WalletConnect methods created, funded and released an escrow on the same node.
On mainnet from the project's test wallet: release, buyer cancel, seller cancel, a dispute decided by two of three panel members, and a release from a seller wallet, 20 transactions.
Run the token escrow on mainnet with PUSD, as it ran on regtest.
Let buyer and seller trade from their own phone wallets over WalletConnect.
A refund to the seller that anyone can trigger after a long deadline, so coins never stay locked.
A signed payment reference from the buyer that the arbitrators can check in a dispute.
